title: DESIGN-PROBES: six probes opened by relaxing three design constraints: drop the anchors, rank per TIER with cost as a router axis, redirect 'specific judges' from prose to references (zero calls)
question: Flat-vs-descent routing on the pool of record (ANCHOR-VALUE); per-cell reference accuracy for two reference sets (REF-BY-CELL); tier recovery at four coarsenesses and five budgets (TIER-RECOVERY); tier-then-cheapest on MMLU-Pro and on the six-corpus union (TIER-ROUTER, TIER-ROUTER-U); a bootstrap self-tiering of the board (TIER-HONEST); registered before looking: does the anchor layer earn its place; does reference accuracy vary enough to select on; how cheap is a tier partition; what does tier-and-cost routing buy.

criteria.text: does the anchor layer earn its place in routing
criteria.value: flat nearest-leaf routing beats the deployed anchor descent on category purity, 0.764 vs 0.753, on the corpus whose own categories ARE the anchors; with the union's 81.6 vs 72.1 that is two corpora in the same direction: the anchor layer is a reporting convenience, not a routing mechanism

criteria.text: does reference accuracy vary enough to select on
criteria.value: per-cell reference SELECTION gains +0.0000 (grok-reasoning beats mistral in all 13 anchors), but grok's own accuracy spans 0.727-0.952 across cells: the design must TRACK reference quality per cell rather than choose between references
nothing to route: best single, per-anchor best and tier-then-cheapest are byte-identical (0.9126, 882 chars) because gemini wins every anchor AND is the cheapest in its tier
tier-then-smallest reaches 0.6143 against per-cell best 0.6169 at 83% of the parameters, and beats best-single 0.5543 by 6.0pp at 53% of the size

criteria.text: how cheap is a tier partition
criteria.value: 0% exact recovery of the key's tier partition at every coarseness and budget (ARI peaks 0.54): the test was the ordering problem in a costume and was rebuilt

across-tier pairs separated 62/64 at 95% with 0 wrong directions, within-tier pairs 2 of 2: the arena is 100% sure iask beats arx and the key says the opposite; self-tiering yields 10 tiers with 2 cross-tier key inversions; a bootstrap CI on a BT strength is confidently wrong exactly where the judge is systematically biased

falsifier.note: a tiered product needs an uncertainty estimate carrying systematic error: the 5.7% test-retest floor, the per-cell reference accuracy, and the free answer-agreement signal are the three candidates already measured

plain_description.what: Six quick probes on cached data. Two compare routing that goes straight to the nearest leaf with routing that descends through the category layer. One measures per-cell accuracy of the reference answers. Three try grouping models into tiers and routing to the cheapest model in a tier. No calls.
plain_description.why: It tests whether three design choices earn their place: the category layer, choosing a reference model, and ranking models strictly.
plain_description.information: Each probe tells the design what to keep or drop. Result: descriptive only. Straight-to-leaf routing is slightly better (0.764 vs 0.753, and 81.6 vs 72.1 on the six-corpus union), so the category layer helps reporting, not routing. Picking a reference per cell gains nothing, but reference accuracy varies (0.73 to 0.95), so it must be tracked. Tier-then-cheapest on the union nearly matches the best per cell with 83% of the parameters. Tiers are not recovered exactly. Bootstrap tiers can be confidently wrong where the judge is biased. Two of the six probes were added after the registration. The reference-per-cell, tier-recovery and bootstrap-tier legs were later ruled 'history, not evidence'. The routing and tier-router legs were not.
